metaDescription: Seven Bissell steam mops compared by scrubbing method, steam settings, pet features and vacuum combos, so you match the right model to your floors.
expertTake: The Spinwave SmartSteam 3897A is the best Bissell for most homes because spinning pads do the scrubbing that you would otherwise do with your wrists. The PowerFresh Pet 19404 is the value pick for small sealed-floor homes that want a plain, proven upright. Anyone with unsealed wood, waxed floors or loose-plank vinyl should skip steam entirely and use a damp microfiber mop.
introParagraphs: A steam mop is a small boiler on a stick. Water flows from a tank into a heating chamber, turns to vapor and is pushed through the mop head into a pad, where heat loosens grease and a cloth lifts it away. Everything else on the spec sheet is a variation on how much steam, how long it lasts and how the pad moves.

One American brand sells steam in nearly every format: plain uprights, spinning-pad models, handheld-convertible kits and machines that vacuum while they steam. The right choice depends less on steam power than on your floor finish, how much scrubbing you want to avoid and whether you also need to pick up crumbs.

products.name: Bissell Spinwave SmartSteam 3897A spinning-pad steam mop
products.description:
The SmartSteam is the only model in this lineup that moves the pads for you. Two round pads spin at up to 230 RPM, which Bissell claims is faster than the leading spinning steam mop, and the steam supplies heat while the rotation supplies the scrubbing stroke. Because the motion happens at the floor, you mostly guide the machine instead of pushing it.

The cost of that design is a motor, a gearbox and a heavier head than the plain uprights here. Fingertip controls let you pick between two steam levels or a no-steam spin mode, so a laminate or luxury vinyl floor can get the gentle setting while a kitchen gets the stronger one. Next to the PowerFresh Deluxe 1806, which relies on a flip-down brush, the SmartSteam covers more floor per minute but is the one to skip if you store your mop in a tight closet.

Upkeep centers on the two pads, which should be rinsed and air dried so mildew does not settle into the fibers. Use clean water in the tank and let the mop cool before you remove the pads, since the head holds heat after you switch off.
products.bestFor: Large kitchens and open floor plans where scrubbing fatigue is the main complaint.
pros: Spinning pads supply the scrubbing stroke
Two steam levels plus a no-steam mode
Swivel steering reaches around furniture legs
LED lights show missed dirt
cons: Heavier head than the plain uprights
Two pads mean more laundry than a single pad

products.name: Bissell PowerFresh Pet 19404 upright steam mop with scent discs
products.description:
This is the plain upright in the family, and that is its charm. A boiler heats water, steam reaches a microfiber pad and a small scrubber flips down to loosen dried drips, with no motors to fail. Bissell adds scent discs that clip into the head, which perfume the steam to cover litter box and wet-dog smells, though they mask rather than remove the source.

The weakness is the same as any pad that you push by hand: you supply the scrubbing force. Compared with the 1940A, which offers three steam settings, this model keeps controls simple, so there is less to adjust and less to explain to a family member. Of the seven machines here it carries the lowest price position, which makes it the logical first steam mop for a rental or a first apartment.

Pet owners should vacuum or sweep before every session, because a steam pad smears fur into streaks. Wash pads after each use without fabric softener, which coats fibers and stops them from soaking up dirt.
products.bestFor: Pet households with sealed tile or vinyl who want the lowest cost of entry.
pros: Lowest price position among the seven
Scent discs help with pet odors
No motor to fail, simple design
Flip-down scrubber lifts dried spots
cons: You supply all the scrubbing force
Scent discs are an ongoing consumable

products.name: Bissell PowerFresh Deluxe 1806 steam mop with SpotBoost brush
products.description:
The Deluxe 1806 is built for floors that get sticky. A bristle brush sits in the head and engages when you press it to the floor, so a burnt-on syrup patch gets a brush stroke and a puff of steam in the same pass. The High and Low switch is the other useful change: Low suits a finish you worry about, High handles the stuck-on patches.

A brush that engages on demand is quicker than hunting for a handheld attachment, yet it cannot reach vertical surfaces. If you want cabinet fronts or window glass, look at the PowerSteamer 2685A instead. The 1806 sits in the middle of the price range, which lands it between the Pet 19404 and the SmartSteam: it adds a brush and two settings, without the motor and weight of the spinning-pad design.

Owners mostly repeat two habits. Fill with distilled water if your tap water leaves white crusts on kettles, because scale narrows the steam outlet and weakens output over a few months. Pull the brush bristles clear of hair once a week so the head sits flat and does not leave a streak line.
products.bestFor: Kitchens and entryways with dried-on spills that need a brush as well as heat.
pros: Brush engages exactly where stuck spots are
High and Low steam suit varied finishes
Ready in about half a minute
Mid-range price for the feature set
cons: Horizontal floors only, no handheld mode
Brush bristles collect hair and need clearing

products.name: Bissell PowerFresh 1940A steam mop with Easy Scrubber
products.description:
Where the other two uprights give you one or two steam choices, the 1940A gives three. That matters on a mixed-floor home: a bottom setting for a finish you do not trust, a middle one for weekly cleaning and the top one for bathroom tile. Bissell also fits a flip-down scrubber meant for grout lines and dried messes.

The extra setting is a controller, not extra boiler power, so it does not out-clean the Deluxe 1806 on a baked-on spill. What it buys is control. At the second-lowest price position in this lineup it is the model I would pick for a house with tile in the wet rooms and sealed wood elsewhere, since you can drop the steam on the wood without changing machines.

After each session, tip out leftover water so the tank does not grow a film, and leave the lid open to dry.
products.bestFor: Mixed homes with tile and sealed wood that need a steam setting per surface.
pros: Three steam levels for mixed floors
Scrubber flips down for grout lines
Second-lowest price position here
Simple controls, no motors
cons: Steam power does not exceed the Deluxe 1806

products.badge: Best Vac and Steam in One
products.name: Bissell PowerFresh Vac and Steam 2747A all-in-one
products.description:
Instead of sweeping and then mopping, the 2747A does both in one pass: a suction nozzle picks up debris just ahead of a steam pad. Touch controls switch between vacuum only, steam only and combined cleaning, so you can run suction alone on a dusty day and add steam when it matters.

Folding two jobs into one frame makes the body bigger than the 1806 or the 1940A, and it asks you to empty a dust bin as well as fill a water tank. It will not match the CrossWave-style wash models for wet messes, because it steams a pad instead of rinsing a roller. The upside is that it never smears crumbs into the pad, which is the usual complaint with an ordinary steam mop.

Keep the vacuum path clear of hair wrap by cutting tangles from the roller every couple of weeks. Empty the dust bin before you add steam, since damp dust cakes onto the filter.
products.bestFor: Homes that want to skip a separate sweep before steaming.
pros: Picks up crumbs before the pad reaches them
Touch controls switch modes without bending
Vacuum-only mode for dry days
One machine replaces broom and mop
cons: Bulkier and heavier than a plain upright
Needs both a dust bin and a tank maintained

products.name: Bissell PowerSteamer Heavy Duty 3-in-1 2685A with SteamShot
products.description:
The 2685A is a convertible. The upright body works as a floor mop, a long-reach steamer for ceilings and high shelves, or a handheld through the SteamShot unit, so the machine is a cleaner for the whole house rather than just the floor.

Versatility is why you would choose it over the PowerFresh models, and tools are what you pay for: more parts to store, more nozzles to lose. Against the Spinwave SmartSteam the PowerSteamer cleans fewer square feet per minute but can reach a stove hood or a shower track that a floor-only model never touches. Reach for it as a deep-clean tool, not a daily mop.

Because hot steam passes through hoses and fittings, inspect the seals before every session and keep the cap threads free of mineral crust. Use a nozzle that fits the job; a narrow jet on painted drywall can lift paint.
products.bestFor: Households that need one machine for floors, grout, appliances and vertical surfaces.
pros: Converts between mop, long-reach and handheld
SteamShot suits grout and appliances
Reaches high and vertical surfaces
Works indoors and on patio items
cons: More attachments to store and keep track of
Slower on large floors than a spin-pad model

products.name: Bissell CrossWave HydroSteam Deluxe 3515G wet-dry vac with steam
products.description:
The HydroSteam Deluxe is a different species from the other mops here. A rotating brushroll washes the floor while a suction path pulls the dirty water into a second tank, and a steam function adds heat to the cleaning solution. Because clean and dirty water never mix, the pass stays fresher than with a pad that you keep rinsing.

That design asks for the largest budget in the lineup and the most upkeep. Compared with the PowerFresh Vac and Steam 2747A, which steams a pad, this one washes with a wet roller and recovers the water, so it handles sticky juice and muddy paw prints that would overwhelm a pad. A tangle-free brushroll resists hair wrap, which suits long-haired pets and people.

Rinse both tanks after each use and leave them open to dry, or a sour smell develops in the recovery tank.
products.bestFor: Large hard-floor homes with pets where a wash-and-recover design beats a pad.
pros: Separate clean and dirty tanks stay fresh
Wet roller and suction pick up sticky spills
Tangle-free brushroll helps with long hair
Combines vacuum, wash and steam
cons: Highest price position of the seven
More tanks and parts to rinse and dry

buyingCriteria.explanation: Steam softens grime but the pad still has to move across the floor. The PowerFresh 1940A and 19404 rely on your push, the 1806 adds a brush that engages under pressure, and the Spinwave SmartSteam spins two pads at up to 230 RPM. Buyers with bad wrists or large floors tend to regret a push-only model within a month.

Steam temperature and flow matter more on wood and laminate than on tile. The 1940A offers three levels, the 1806 and SmartSteam offer two, and the 19404 keeps controls simple. A low setting leaves less moisture behind, which matters because water that creeps into a seam is how warping begins.

A plain steam mop does not pick up debris, so you sweep first. The 2747A vacuums and steams at once, and the CrossWave HydroSteam Deluxe 3515G washes with a roller and recovers dirty water. Both are heavier and need more rinsing than a stick mop. If you already own a good stick vacuum, a plain upright is the lighter path.

The PowerSteamer 2685A is the only model here that converts to a handheld and long-reach steamer through the SteamShot. That reach is what cleans grout, stove hoods and shower doors. The tradeoff is storage and loose attachments, so buy it only if you will actually use the vertical tools. Otherwise a floor-only mop is faster to grab and put away.

The 1806 is listed at about 30 seconds to heat, a figure typical of a small boiler. Tank size sets how many rooms you finish before a refill, and a tank you can refill mid-job without unplugging saves time. Hard tap water leaves scale in the boiler, so plan on distilled water if the faucet leaves crust on your kettle. Scale slowly cuts steam output.

Steam mops are for sealed tile, sealed hardwood, sealed laminate and similar finishes, and the maker's floor list on the box is the best signal. Unsealed wood, waxed floors and loose-plank vinyl can swell, haze or lose adhesive. A quick check is whether a water drop beads on the surface. When in doubt, read the flooring warranty for steam language.

specDecoder.meaning: Revolutions per minute describes how fast the pads rotate against the floor. Higher speed means more scrubbing strokes per second.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SmartSteam's up to 230 RPM is a ceiling, and the pad load and floor texture decide what you feel.

specDecoder.meaning: Settings control how much vapor reaches the pad per second, not always the vapor temperature. More levels let you protect delicate finishes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 1940A gives three levels while the 1806 and SmartSteam give two.

specDecoder.meaning: This is how long the boiler takes to produce usable steam after you switch on. Smaller boilers heat faster but may hold less water.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 1806 lists about 30 seconds; treat it as a best case with room-temperature water.

specDecoder.meaning: Separate clean and dirty tanks keep recovered water from re-wetting the floor. It is a feature of wash-and-recover machines, not of plain steam mops.
specDecoder.watchFor: The 3515G uses this layout, which also means two tanks to rinse and dry.

specDecoder.meaning: Percentages on the box apply only under the maker's stated conditions, such as a named organism and a set contact time. Steam cleaning is not a disinfectant registration.
specDecoder.watchFor: Read the footnote on any Bissell claim and follow its dwell time before trusting it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Scrubbing mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each mop applies friction: push-only pad, flip-down scrubber, engaging brush, spinning pads or wet roller. The spinning-pad SmartSteam and the roller-based 3515G ranked higher on effort saved. A lineup with every mechanism lets you pick the one that suits your wrists.

howWeEvaluated.title: Floor safety controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at steam-level choices and the maker's stated floor list. The 1940A's three levels earned credit for finish protection. Models with fewer settings were rated on how clearly the box describes sealed-floor limits.

howWeEvaluated.title: Versatility beyond the floor
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether a model converts to a handheld or long-reach tool. Only the PowerSteamer 2685A does through the SteamShot, so it scored well here even though it is slower on large floors. This category matters most to people who clean grout and appliances.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed the rinsing, drying and part-tracking each design asks for. Plain uprights such as the 19404 need only pad washing, while the 3515G needs two tanks and a brushroll cleaned. Fewer parts won where cleaning power was similar.

howWeEvaluated.title: Price position across the family
howWeEvaluated.description: We used relative price tiers from the listings, from the cheapest 19404 up to the 3515G at the top, without quoting any figure. Value was judged by what each step up adds: a scrubber, extra settings, a motor or a vacuum. A step that adds nothing you use is wasted money.

cards.label: Steam pad
cards.text: A pad machine such as the 1940A or the 2747A uses heat and a cloth. It is light, quick to start and cheap to run, but the pad can smear fine dust and has to be washed. It suits light messes on sealed floors.

cards.label: Wet roller
cards.text: The HydroSteam Deluxe 3515G washes with a rotating roller and pulls dirty water into a second tank. It cleans sticky spills better but demands tank rinsing. It suits pets, kids and big floors.

howToChoose.note: Pick the 1940A or 19404 for light weekly mopping; pick the 3515G if mud and juice are the daily problem.

rows: SteamShot handheld reaches what a floor head cannot
Dry crumbs and wet mess together
Vacuum runs ahead of the steam pad

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Hair control and odor handling. Fur wraps brushes, and a steam pad pushes it into streaks, so either a vacuum stage or a tangle-resistant roller helps. Scent discs only mask smells and do not fix the source.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The CrossWave HydroSteam Deluxe 3515G has a tangle-free brushroll and two tanks. The PowerFresh Pet 19404 is the budget answer, with scent discs, but you must sweep first.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean large floors weekly, have bad wrists or have pets. The Spinwave SmartSteam 3897A and the CrossWave 3515G reduce effort and handle sticky, repeated messes better than a plain pad.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your floors are small and sealed, and you mop once a week. The 19404 or the 1940A do the same boiler job for a lower price position.

maintenance.why: Dirt left in a damp pad grows odor. Air dry it flat, and skip fabric softener, which coats the fibers.

maintenance.interval: Every fill if tap water is hard
maintenance.why: Mineral scale builds in the boiler and narrows the steam outlet. Distilled water avoids the crust that cuts steam output.
Hair wraps the SpotBoost brush and the roller of the vacuum models, lifting the head off the floor. A quick cut keeps contact even.
Standing water breeds film. The dirty tank on the 3515G especially smells within days if sealed wet.
A worn seal can leak hot water or steam at the cap. Replace damaged parts before the next session.

faq.q: Which Bissell steam mop is best for pet owners?
faq.a: For a low budget, the PowerFresh Pet 19404 with scent discs is the plain answer, provided you sweep first. For heavier pet mess the CrossWave HydroSteam Deluxe 3515G washes with a roller and recovers dirty water. Scent discs mask odor and do not remove the source.

faq.q: Is a spinning-pad steam mop worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you mop large floors weekly, yes, because the pads supply the scrubbing stroke. If your floor is small and lightly soiled, the 1940A or the 19404 cleans just as well at a lower price position.

faq.q: Can I use a Bissell steam mop on any floor?
faq.a: No. Use it on sealed tile, sealed hardwood and similar finishes that the box lists. Unsealed wood, waxed floors and some vinyl plank can swell or lose adhesive. Check your flooring warranty for steam language, and test a hidden corner first.

faq.q: Does steam really kill 99.9 percent of germs?
faq.a: The claim is tied to a footnote with a named organism and a contact time. A mop that glides quickly across the floor may not hold the pad long enough. Treat steam as chemical-free cleaning, not as hospital-grade disinfection.

faq.q: How long does a Bissell steam mop last?
faq.a: Plain uprights with no motors tend to wear out at the cord, seals or pad strip. Scale in the boiler is the most common killer, so use distilled water if your tap leaves crust. Models with motors, like the SmartSteam, add a gearbox as a wear point.

faq.q: Is a vacuum and steam combo better than a separate vacuum?
faq.a: It saves one pass, but the combined body is bulkier and has more parts to rinse. If you already own a light stick vacuum, a plain steam mop is faster to start. A combo makes sense when you hate sweeping first.
